title: Maharashtra Declares Drought in 305 Talukas, Promises Farmers Rs 5,000 Before Diwali
excerpt: Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis added 40 talukas to the drought list, taking coverage past 85 percent of the state, and said the Rs 5,000 assistance will be credited before Diwali without waiting for central assessment.
body:
• Maharashtra has declared drought in 305 of its 358 talukas, after adding 40 more talukas to the 265 announced last month.
  • Farmers in the drought-affected talukas will receive Rs 5,000 each, credited directly to their bank accounts before Diwali.
  • All 12 standard state drought relief concessions now extend to the newly added talukas, alongside crop loan restructuring and land revenue waivers.
  • The state has also authenticated a further 3.5 lakh farmers for scheduled debt relief payments, and warned banks against coercive loan recovery.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday declared drought in 305 of the state's 358 talukas and announced that farmers will receive Rs 5,000 each in their bank accounts before Diwali as immediate assistance. The declaration adds 40 talukas to the 265 declared drought-affected last month, meaning more than 85 percent of the state's talukas are now classified as drought-hit, according to Livemint.

Fadnavis said the advance payment was necessary because the full administrative process, including central assessment, would take time and could not legally be completed before the festival. The state, he said, was not waiting for that process to conclude before putting money in farmers' hands.

"This Diwali is going to be difficult for farmers."

— Devendra Fadnavis, Chief Minister of Maharashtra

How the Drought List Grew

The government first declared 265 talukas drought-affected last month, citing a rainfall deficit, and announced relief measures including restructuring crop loans, waiving land revenue and subsidising electricity bills. Following complaints and a review, officials identified 40 more talukas for inclusion, and a supplementary Government Resolution has been issued to formalise the expansion, Fadnavis told reporters after the cabinet meeting, as reported by Devdiscourse (ANI).

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2110314986807689428

The timing is earlier than usual. Drought declarations are generally made by the end of November, with assistance following from December, the chief minister noted. This year the notification was brought forward to October because of the severity of the situation, and all 12 standard state drought relief concessions now apply in the added talukas as well.

Water, Debt and Power Relief

Beyond the Diwali payment, the state has processed an authenticated list of another 3.5 lakh farmers eligible for scheduled debt relief, Fadnavis said, and loan waiver amounts are also being credited to accounts. District Central Co-operative banks and credit societies have been warned against pressuring farmers to repay loans or using coercive recovery practices, and the government is working to extend similar directions to private banks and financial institutions.

Two older provisions have also been loosened. An outdated clause in a 1992 resolution that limited educational fee waivers for farmers' children has been removed, so the exemption now applies universally across drought-affected areas. On power, farmers are protected from coercive action over outstanding electricity bills, and agricultural pumps up to 7.5 horsepower are eligible for free electricity under state policy.

The water situation is tightening in parallel. Groundwater levels in observation wells across Marathwada have dropped below 3 metres, and the government is preparing to deploy drinking water tankers as early as October and November, with every tanker monitored through GPS tracking. Nearly 16,000 illegal water connections have been disconnected, and fodder availability currently ranges from 90 days to seven months depending on the region. The state has assured farmers it will purchase harvested fodder at the Minimum Support Price, and has encouraged farmers with irrigation access to grow rabi jowar and fodder crops.

What Happens Next

For farming families with relatives in the diaspora, the immediate checkpoint is simple: the Rs 5,000 should land in the farmer's bank account before Diwali, without waiting for the central assessment to finish. Families remitting money for the festival can factor that confirmed state payment into what they send.

The larger relief package will still run through the normal channel, including the central assessment Fadnavis said could not be completed before the festival. The state cabinet, at the same meeting, also passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Narendra Modi on completing 25 years as head of government. Attention in Maharashtra, however, will stay on delivery: whether the Diwali transfers arrive on schedule in all 305 talukas, and how tanker deployment holds up as groundwater continues to fall.
